00:00–00:12: A sustained, resonant bell tone, low to mid-pitch, with a slow decay and natural reverb, fills the audio space. No speech or other sounds are present.

00:12–00:13: The bell tone ends abruptly. A male voice begins speaking, clear and calm, with no noticeable echo or background noise.

00:13–00:22: “Nirvana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop.”

00:22–00:30: “The letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you anymore, stopping.”

00:30–00:38: “Going out like a flame with no fuel.”

00:38–00:45: “This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.”

00:45–00:47: A brief pause. No speech or ambient sound.

00:47–00:50: “Why don’t I see Nirvana right now?”

00:50–00:58: “You do not see Nirvana right now, because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there.”

00:58–01:07: “What is called ‘manana’ is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things.”

01:07–01:15: “Only a looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen.”

01:15–01:24: “The law of dependent arising is already implicated. There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

01:24–01:26: A brief pause. No speech or ambient sound.

01:26–01:34: “What keeps it going? Thirst keeps it going, impelled by that making it into something, it runs towards the mirage, the gap is ignored.”

01:34–01:42: “What impels one to ignore that gap is thirst. Perception. What impels one to ignore that gap is craving.”

01:42–01:44: A brief pause. No speech or ambient sound.

01:44–01:53: “How is the sense of self constructed? The sense of self is constructed like this: when one looks into a mirror, one suddenly becomes self-conscious.”

01:53–02:02: “Even with no such notion, the moment one looks, one is reminded of it, as if to exclaim, ‘Ah, here I am.’”

02:02–02:10: “Even if one already has no such notion, the moment one looks into a mirror, one is suddenly reminded of it, as if to exclaim, ‘Ah, here I am.’”

02:10–02:18: “This is the gist of what Ven. Punnamantani Buddha is trying to put across through this discourse. This shows that the conceit ‘I’ arises due to the five grasping groups.”

02:18–02:20: A brief pause. No speech or ambient sound.

02:20–02:28: “How is Nirvana attained? Nirvana is only attained now, in seeing, just the seeing, with no ‘I’ added, then it will not carry you.”

02:28–02
